pois.name: Coral-habitat ledge
pois.note: The GMRT grid reads 941.9 m at this canyon-flank marker. NOAA's September 2025 Global Explorer expedition documented Hudson Canyon's coral and sponge habitats, but does not establish a coral colony or protection-area boundary at this exact coordinate. The placed coral mound's position and layout are authored; reconstruction remains true. Regional fisheries protection restricts most bottom-tending commercial gear, with lobster and deep-sea red crab trap exceptions; the Council's corrected area is about 41,440 sq mi.

pois.name: Canyon flank transect
pois.note: Real GMRT terrain: 947.2 m deep at the centre of row 432, column 947 (zero-based) in data/tiles/hudson-canyon/heightmap.bin. This terrain survey is about 280 m north of the coral-habitat ledge marker (moved 2026-11 from 555 m north-west so the dive is a short route). The GMRT grid reads about 947 m here, compared with about 942 m at the ledge marker. The nearby pair samples the surveyed canyon flank. This point was chosen from the terrain grid for the dive; it does not mark a documented coral colony.

pois.name: North wall of the upper canyon
pois.note: Real GMRT terrain (Ryan et al. 2009; value and slope read directly from this tile's grid this session): 541.9 m deep, on a locally steep flank of the upper canyon's north wall. Central-difference slope sampling over one grid cell (~50-60 m) gives roughly 18-19 deg here -- steep for this ~50 m grid, and the true wall relief (rock outcrops and ledges per MAFMC's habitat description) is almost certainly sharper than this coarse sampling can resolve.

pois.name: Canyon flank, toward the axis
pois.note: Real GMRT terrain at about 977 m, south-east of the flank transect where the seabed falls toward the canyon's axis. Added 2026-11 as a route stop for the guide's 'Down the axis' entry; the entry's depth figures come from the north-wall, upper-floor and deepest-cell readings, not from this point.

pois.name: Proposed sanctuary waters
pois.note: GMRT terrain at about 928 m on the canyon flank, between the coral ledge and the flank transect. Hudson Canyon is the area NOAA proposes for a national marine sanctuary; no boundary is designated, so this marker stands for the canyon as a whole, not a boundary point. Added 2026-11 as a route stop.
